preamble: Nasalization of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the palatal nasal [ɲ] occurs in Jê languages of Brazil, where voiced stops and nasals form a single series whose nasality is determined by the syllable nucleus. In Proto-Northern Jê the voiced palatal stop */ɟ/ (written *ĵ, and *ñ before nasal vowels) was realized as [ɲ] before nasal nuclei, as [ɟ] in stressed oral syllables and as [j] in unstressed oral ones.

examples.from: *ñõt 'to sleep' (nonfinite), underlying */ɟ/ before the nasal nucleus õ
examples.note: The onset */ɟ/ is realized nasal [ɲ] before nasal nuclei, oral [ɟ] in stressed oral syllables (*ĵər, nonfinite of *ga 'to roast') and [j] in unstressed oral syllables.

examples.from: *ñõr 'to give' (nonfinite), underlying */ɟ/ before the nasal nucleus õ
*ñõpôk 'to pierce', underlying */ɟ/ before the nasal nucleus õ
